tagline: Detached work isn't a live thread you watch — it runs **out-of-line** and **notifies on completion**.
summary: Claude Code can run work **detached** from the foreground turn. A forked agent runs in the **background** so the parent keeps going; a shell command can run as a **background session** you attach to and detach from; and a whole session can be launched headless with `claude --bg --exec`. The common thread: detached work is **not a live feed**. Its tool output stays **out of the parent's context**, and you get a **completion notification**, not a window into every step.

sections.heading: Foreground vs detached
body: In the **foreground**, every tool call and its output land in the current turn — you see them as they happen. **Detached** execution breaks that coupling: the work proceeds **independently**, and the parent is free to keep working instead of blocking on it.

This is the same machinery as an **agent fork**: a fork "runs in the background" precisely so its heavy exploration doesn't stall — or flood — the parent. Background execution generalizes that to shell commands and to entire sessions.

sections.heading: The surfaces
body: **Pinned background sessions** (`Ctrl+T` in `claude agents`) stay alive when idle and are restarted in place to apply updates. Typing **`! <command>`** runs a shell command as a background session you can **attach to and detach from**. And **`claude --bg --exec '<command>'`** launches a detached session headlessly from the start.

In every case the contract is the same as a fork's: the detached worker's intermediate tool output **does not stream into the parent's context**. What crosses back is a **result and a notification** — not a live transcript.

sections.heading: Notification, not a feed
body: The mental model that breaks is "a background agent is a second thread I can watch scroll by." It is **detached**: you are told when it **finishes** (and can attach to inspect it), but you are not subscribed to every step in real time.
That's a feature — it's what keeps a long, tool-heavy job from **drowning the parent's context window**. The parent stays lean; the conclusion arrives when it's ready.

diagram.caption: Detached work runs **out-of-line**. Its tool output stays in its own context; the parent gets a **notification**, not a live feed.

nodes.label: Foreground session
nodes.note: The turn you're in. Foreground tool calls and their output land here, visible as they happen.

nodes.label: Foreground or detached?
nodes.note: Run inline (output in this turn), or **detach** it: a background fork, a `! <command>` session, or `claude --bg --exec`.

nodes.label: Detached worker
nodes.note: Runs **independently** of the foreground turn. Pinned sessions (Ctrl+T) survive idle; `! <command>` sessions can be attached and detached.

nodes.label: Tool output stays out-of-line
nodes.note: Every read, search, and build runs in the **worker's** context — it does **not** stream into the parent's context window.

nodes.label: Completion notification
nodes.note: The parent is **notified when the work finishes** — not subscribed to every step. You can attach to inspect the result.

scenarios.title: Detach a long job and **keep working** in the foreground
scenarios.note: The parent doesn't block. The worker's tool output never floods the foreground context — only the **completion notification** arrives.

scenarios.title: Launch a headless session with **--bg --exec**
scenarios.note: `claude --bg --exec '<command>'` starts the session detached from the outset — no foreground turn to watch it scroll.

misconceptions.myth: A background agent is a live parallel thread I can watch scroll by.
misconceptions.reality: It's **detached**. You get a **completion notification** and can attach to inspect it — you are not subscribed to every step as it happens.
misconceptions.why: "Running in parallel" suggests a second live feed. The point of detaching is to keep the parent's context clean, so the steps are deliberately out-of-line.

misconceptions.myth: A background agent's tool output ends up in my main conversation.
misconceptions.reality: The detached worker's reads, searches, and build output stay in **its own context**. The parent receives the result, not the intermediate output.
misconceptions.why: It's the same boundary a fork has — heavy exploration is hidden on purpose so it can't drown the parent's context window.

misconceptions.myth: Closing or moving on from the foreground turn kills the background work.
misconceptions.reality: Detached sessions run **independently** — pinned background sessions (Ctrl+T) even stay alive when idle and restart in place to apply updates.
misconceptions.why: Foreground tool output is coupled to the turn, so it feels like everything is. Detaching is exactly what decouples the work's lifetime from the turn.
